Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[Rick Scott]] won a second term, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Debbie Mucarsel-Powell]]. The primary election was held on August 20, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Scott, then the [[governor of Florida]], was first elected to the U.S. Senate in [[2018 United States Senate election in Florida|2018]] by 0.12 points, defeating then-incumbent [[Bill Nelson]].{{Cite web |title=Florida {{!}} Full Senate results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2018/results/florida |access-date=2023-04-16 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} With the benefit of incumbency and the state's rightward trend, most political pundits considered the race to be favoring Scott to win re-election. On Election Day, Scott won by 12.78 percentage points, a significantly larger margin than most pre-election polls had suggested. Out of all of Scott’s four statewide races (2010 and 2014 gubernatorial elections, 2018 and 2024 senatorial elections), this election was by far his best performance, and the first one he won decisively, as he narrowly won the previous three all by less than a 2% margin. Scott won [[List of majority-Hispanic or Latino counties in the United States|majority-Hispanic]] [[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade]] and [[Osceola County, Florida|Osceola]] counties, as well as [[St. Lucie County, Florida|St. Lucie County]] for the first time in all of his statewide races, and according to exit polls Scott won 55% of Hispanic voters and also won 21% of African American voters.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2024/exit-polls/florida/general/us-senate/0|title=Election 2024: Exit polls|website=CNN}} {{TOC limit|3}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Rick Scott]], incumbent U.S. senator (2019–present){{Cite web |last=Caputo |first=Marc |date=2023-01-26 |title=Sen.
